correctness.rationale: For each fixed pattern, greedy embedding times are independent geometric variables with generating factors g_{letter}, and the cumulative occurrence series is their product divided by 1-z. Every even palindrome is uniquely v reverse(v) and every odd palindrome v a reverse(v), giving V^j and U V^j and hence the stated rational formal series without counting positional multiplicity. Positive coefficients and aperiodicity give a unique positive dominant simple pole r in (0,1), V(r)=1, with the displayed residue. At z=4/5 the exact identity pi_a-[4pi_a/(1+4pi_a)]^2=pi_a(4pi_a-1)^2/(1+4pi_a)^2 >=0 yields V(4/5)<=1, hence r>=4/5, with equality only pi_a=1/4 for every supported symbol and thus exactly four letters. Direct rational word/mask enumeration independently matched the coefficients for 29 finite tests and checked sharp test families. This proves the all-finite-alphabet bound analytically rather than experimentally.

originality.rationale: Biers-Ariel–Godbole–Kelley treat mean distinct scattered subsequences without a palindromic restriction; Mahalingam–Pandoh treat deterministic scattered palindrome counts and Rubinchik–Shur treat random contiguous palindromic factors. Their different counts cannot simply be substituted to yield the full series and universal sharp source optimization. No stronger identified primary result asserts this extremum. A generic weighted-language formula could implicitly include the first rational identity; this risk is recorded.

value.rationale: Distinct scattered palindromes combine a natural inverse-subsequence pattern statistic with random-source weighting. The exact first-moment rational series and a uniquely optimizing alphabet cardinality, independent of any finite alphabet bound, give a sharp new extremal phenomenon (5/4) that is neither a deterministic maximum nor a contiguous-palindrome statistic.

final_claim: For any iid finite positive-support letter law, the expected number of distinct nonempty palindromic scattered subsequence strings has exact ordinary generating function (U+V)/((1-z)(1-V)), U=sum g_a and V=sum g_a^2 with g_a=pi_a z/(1-(1-pi_a)z); its growth base is at most 5/4, equality only for four equiprobable letters, when the expectation is asymptotic to 3(5/4)^n.
limitations: Mean only, not variance, concentration, almost sure growth or Markov sources.
Finite computational cross-checks are not the proof of the global optimization.
